definitions.explanation: The state of something or someone truly existing in reality, as opposed to being fictional, legendary, or hypothetical.

examples.japanese: {実在|じつざい}の{人物|じんぶつ}をモデルにした。
examples.english: It was modeled on a real person.

examples.japanese: この{物語|ものがたり}は{実在|じつざい}する{事件|じけん}に{基|もと}づいている。
examples.english: This story is based on a real incident.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}が{本当|ほんとう}に{実在|じつざい}したかどうかは、{歴史家|れきしか}の{間|あいだ}でも{意見|いけん}が{分|わ}かれている。
examples.english: Whether he truly existed is a matter of debate even among historians.

notes:
{実在|じつざい} combines {実|じつ} (actual, real) and {在|ざい} (existence). It can function as a noun or as a suru verb ({実在|じつざい}する).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {実在|じつざい}の{人物|じんぶつ} (real person)
- {実在|じつざい}する{場所|ばしょ} (real place)
- {実在|じつざい}が{確認|かくにん}される (existence is confirmed)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {存在|そんざい} is the general word for existence, while {実在|じつざい} specifically emphasizes being real as opposed to fictional or imaginary.
